mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the previous 20-day window with similar FEDFUNDS path (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% in a month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the combined PAYEMS/UNRATE signal (Spearman's rho < 0.2, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1.5% suggests expanding credit availability and consumer confidence, which accelerates equity market valuation growth and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 30 consecutive 20-day windows with HOUST growth > 1%, 20-day forward returns are not higher than the median of non-expansion periods (Mann-Whitney U p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 2% indicates softening supply-side constraints, which reduces production costs and improves profit margins, thereby supporting equity valuations and generating positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 95th percentile of INDPRO-stable periods (rolling quantile regression, p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive months during a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit negative 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate rate hikes that erode equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day window with similar CPIAUCSL path (Granger causality p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% triggers a wage-price spiral, increasing labor costs for firms and reducing profit margins, which depresses S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from the prior 5-day window with UNRATE above 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining federal funds rates below 1% indicate central bank accommodation, lowering real interest rates and stimulating risk appetite, which typically produces positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the FEDFUNDS trend (Spearman's rho < 0.15, p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains flat for three consecutive months while other demand proxies (GDPC1, PAYEMS) show expansion, it suggests supply-side bottlenecks persist, depressing equity valuations and generating negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by > 2% while PAYEMS increases by > 1% and INDPRO remains flat for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not lower than during the prior 20-day window with similar multi-proxy pattern (Mann-Whitney U p > 0.05).
